precepts.why:
“Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon? Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.”

Right here we are going back: chapter 26 picks this thread back up. Again “the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?”

And again Saul went down “to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him.” “But David abode in the wilderness”, and he “sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.”

moments.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat
Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: These dudes was itching to get it on. David had to hold back their hands. These dudes were some warriors, man. And they even had the weapon of choice, the spear: I got it right here on me, please let me let loose. And David was like, nah, don't do that.

Even though the spirit of the Lord departed from Saul and an evil spirit inhabited his fleshly body and his mind, King David still understood that this man was chosen before me. Who am I to touch him? Absolutely not. Let God deal with him. That's what happens when you walking in the spirit.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: This is when Saul was hunting David to kill him, because Saul was dealing with bitterness, envy, and hatred. David and Abishai came down to the camp by night, and Saul lay sleeping in the trench, with Abner, the top warrior in Israel at that time, and the people round about him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless? Saul was anointed by the Lord to be king, and David understood: I cannot kill one of God's anointed. That is the kind of love David had toward his people.

Even in your marriage: sometimes Satan will jump on a brother and he will say evil things to his wife; sister, you have to realize it is not your husband, it is Satan you are really dealing with. Remember when Satan entered Job's wife: curse God, and die. Job said, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. Job was not dealing with her; he was dealing with what entered into her and was speaking.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: As the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish. The Lord is the one that is going to deal with Saul if he does not change. That is the same state of mind we all have to have: even if somebody does you wrong, you do not have to do evil back. Sometimes it is good to leave it in God's hands. David took the spear and the cruse of water, went far off on a hill, and called out.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: I have seen people in the body spread evil, even about me: brothers going to brothers saying the Deacon said this and that, and brothers end up hating me off of a whisper. A couple years back there were a couple of wormtongue brothers just whispering and murmuring, and I sat back and watched. Once I find one bitter, murmuring brother, everybody in that circle is defiled, because the scripture says if a man purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour. If a brother is bitter against leadership because he got corrected, and you are around him buddy buddy, it is because you all have the same spirit. That is why I do not rush to get rid of bitter brothers; I leave them for a while and see who gravitates to them.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand? If the Lord have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering. Sometimes the Lord can put a spirit on somebody to do something to you, to see how you operate; and how you deal with it tells whether you get the kingdom or not. That person might deal with you wrongfully, but it is really to try you. If you become bitter and deal with it wrong, you lose the kingdom, while the Lord may forgive the one who wronged you. Remember Shimei cursing David: David said, let him alone; the Lord hath bidden him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: But if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the Lord. What was taking place with Saul? You had men around Saul whispering in his ears: David thinks he is better than you; David wants the kingdom. Satan was in certain men around Saul, and Saul was feeding into it instead of saying, I do not want to hear that; David would never do that; David is a man of God. That is why you better be vigilant: if somebody comes and whispers evil to you, ask them, why are you coming to say this to me? You want me to hate that person? Did you correct that person?

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David... behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. David hit a nerve, and Saul caught himself. Sometimes people do evil to you because Satan jumped on them, and afterward they realize it and say, I am sorry. When somebody comes at you sideways, it is not necessarily the person in front of you that you are fighting; it is Satan in them.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: As thy life was much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation. That is what you want: the Lord to deliver you out of tribulations. But you do not want to take vengeance into your own hands, and that is what David understood.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: The Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon? Right here we are going back: chapter 26 is picking up on what we read in chapter 23, when the Ziphites first went up to Saul to deliver David into the king's hand.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, and pitched in the hill of Hachilah; but David abode in the wilderness, sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David beheld the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host; Saul lay in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster, and the people pitched round about him as protection to the king.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day; let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless?

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David left Saul's end with the Most High: as the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall descend into battle and perish; the Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: They took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster and got them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David went over to the other side, stood on the top of an hill afar off, and cried to Abner: Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: As the Lord liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord's anointed; and now see where the king's spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Saul knew David's voice and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Saul said, I have sinned: return, my son David, for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. Saul was acknowledging once more David's righteousness, because again David had an opportunity to kill Saul and did not put forth his hand.

That is what we have to get to as far as brotherly love: when we see each other, we see Christ in each other. That is what our nation is lacking, and that is why we have to be that example, as David was in sparing Saul's life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: David answered, The Lord render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed. Again he showed compassion, restraint, and the fear of the Most High.
